items.t: Meta opens early access program for new Muse features
items.d: Anyone interested in joining has to ask Muse to put them on the list.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 1:34 PM PDT · September 25, 2026 Image Credits: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto (opens in a new window) / Getty Images Sarah Perez Meta opens early access program for new Muse features After announcing a host of new features for Meta’s Muse AI app at its Connect 2026 developer conference this week, the company is opening up requests for early access. Meta shared on Friday that you can now ask Muse to put you on the list to try out its latest capabilities before anyone else. Meta posted a link to a prompt on X that, when shared with Muse, will log that you’re interested in joining Meta’s early access program. Just announced lots of new features…want early access? Your Muse can ask for you. Click below to drop a prompt into Muse👇 https://t.co/wI5YXmz50b — Muse (@Muse) September 25, 2026 (If you don’t want to click through, you can just copy and paste the prompt: “Can you let the Muse team know I want to be part of the Muse early access program?”) While typically companies offer pilot tests or betas with select users, they often A/B test with a randomized group to gain feedback and measure results. In this case, however, Meta is looking for AI enthusiasts to try its features first. That tactic could help it stay ahead of the competition, given that this crowd tends to use multiple AI apps and agents and has a good understanding of the market. As to what the new features will be? Meta teased many of those at Connect, including the launch of a digital avatar for Muse that you’ll be able to video chat with, tons more shopping partnerships and connectors, and an expansion of the Muse Mac app, which will soon be able to use your computer to complete various tasks. The company also said that Muse would be coming to Meta’s lineup of AI glasses , so users can interact with the agent just by speaking a wake word, then issuing a command. items.t: Mark Wahlberg is coming to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, and he wants to talk about your work, not his
items.d: Mark Wahlberg joins Bruce K. Lee at Disrupt to discuss investing, entrepreneurship, healthcare, wellness, and building businesses.
items.fullText: Let’s just get this out of the way: Mark Wahlberg is as A-list as it gets. He broke out in 1997’s “Boogie Nights,” and in the nearly three decades since, he’s built one of the highest-wattage careers in Hollywood: two Academy Award nominations, a Golden Globe nod for “The Fighter,” multiple Emmy nominations as a producer (HBO’s “Entourage” among them), and a filmography that spans crime dramas, comedies, and action blockbusters. Right now, he’s back on-screen in “By Any Means,” a manhunt thriller set during the 1966 Mississippi civil rights killings. He’s also signaling where he’s increasingly turning his attention. Wahlberg will sit down with Bruce K. Lee , founder and CEO of Keebeck Wealth Management , on the main stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 to talk about that progression. Grab your ticket here so you don’t miss a moment of this session and Disrupt 2026. Ticket prices increase when the clock strikes 11:59 p.m. PT tonight. Image Credits: TechCrunch From Hollywood to business venture His acting career is really just part of the picture. Over the past two decades, Wahlberg has built a production company, a restaurant chain, apparel and fitness ventures, a slate of angel investments, and the now-25-year-old Mark Wahlberg Youth Foundation, which supports inner-city kids and teens. He’s used his Hollywood success to launch big projects well outside the movie business — and in a fireside chat at this year’s Disrupt, he’s going to give us a peek into how. Building an investing mindset Wahlberg, who’s leaned almost entirely on entrepreneurial instinct about people, culture, products, and markets, is now someone who’s been building institutional-level investing discipline, with Lee as his guide, and with a growing focus on healthcare and wellness startups. items.t: Meadow lets you leave your smartphone at home without sacrificing the essentials
items.d: “We’re not Luddites... it’s just we don’t want social media, browsing, and that kind of stuff," said 25-year-old founder Shreyas Narlanka.
items.fullText: I held my breath as I walked into the concert venue and showed the bouncer a ticket barcode on a three-inch, square screen. “If it doesn’t go through, I can try something else,” I said quickly, worried that the barcode wouldn’t work. But just as Meadow founder Shreyas Narlanka promised me, the code I scanned onto the startup’s minimalist phone earlier that day worked fine. “Cool phone,” the bouncer said, ushering me inside. I’d done it. With Meadow’s bare-bones smartphone, I had called an Uber, streamed Apple Music during the ride, and entered the show. Not once did I need to touch my iPhone, which I only brought with me as a backup in case the ticket scan didn’t work. “With so many dumb phones, the Brick , and everything, the messaging is like, ‘Slow down, focus on your work’ or whatever,” Narlanka says, explaining why his company chose to build a minimal phone. “But the reason we’re different is because we’re all about getting outside and unplugging and having a sick social life.” Image Credits: Meadow Go online, and you’ll see a growing mass of content and comments from people across the world feeling suffocated by being constantly connected via their smartphones and social media feeds. That’s resulting in a new device category that promises a reprieve. Some of these devices, like the Light Phone , require users to completely give up their smartphone and switch to a simpler device. Others, like the Wisephone , offer a modern touchscreen device with a minimal UI and a few apps. Still others are embracing more tactile form factors, like the Commodore Callback , which is a flip-phone with a touchscreen. Meadow, meanwhile, is taking the middle road, intending to simply supplement your existing device. It runs Android, and so supports apps like Maps, Strava, Uber, Apple Music, and Spotify. items.t: Bill Gates says AI companies self-regulating isn’t enough and governments should be involved
items.d: Bill Gates called for lawmakers in Washington to regulate the development of artificial intelligence, weeks after the CEOs of some of the nation’s biggest AI labs agreed on the need to slow the pace of AI progress.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Bill Gates says AI companies self-regulating isn’t enough and governments should be involved in monitoring The Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist said AI is capable of helping bad actors harm billions of people. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Add to Google Bill Gates says AI 'powerful enough' to cause 'a billion deaths' 01:18 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 25, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT By Alexandra Marquez Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates on Wednesday called for lawmakers in Washington to regulate the development of artificial intelligence, weeks after the CEOs of some of the nation’s biggest AI labs agreed on the need to slow the pace of AI progress. “No one thinks self-regulation is enough,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” in an interview set to air in full Sunday. Asked by moderator Kristen Welker whether there needs to be legislation passed in Washington, Gates said, “Absolutely.” “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like,” he said. “And that has to be a required thing. And it will be a little bit of overhead for the industry, but not a dramatic slowing of what they’re doing.” Earlier this month, the CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the nation’s biggest AI labs, agreed that the race to develop powerful AI systems should slow down . Their statements on the issue came after a whistleblower who recently resigned from Anthropic, Jacob Coxon, publicly declared that “neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon added in a series of social media posts and interviews that week. items.fullText: 이코노미 > 경제 AI 투자축 GPU서 CPU·메모리로 확장…판 뒤집힌다 “삼전닉스 가치 재평가” 발행일 : 2026-09-25 19:15 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 삼성전자(왼쪽)와 SK하이닉스. 사진=연합뉴스 KB증권, AI 에이전트 확산으로 메모리 수요 확대 전망 인공지능(AI) 인프라 투자의 중심축이 그래픽처리장치(GPU)에서 중앙처리장치(CPU)와 메모리 반도체로 빠르게 이동하면서 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 전략적 가치가 재평가될 수 있다는 분석이 나왔다. AI 에이전트 확산으로 추론 연산이 늘어나면서 고대역폭메모리(HBM)는 물론 DDR5와 기업용 솔리드스테이트드라이브(eSSD)까지 AI 데이터센터 전반의 메모리 수요가 확대될 수 있다는 전망이다. 김동원 KB증권 리서치본부장은 지난 24일 최근 뉴욕 증시에서 인텔, AMD, ARM 등의 주가가 급등한 배경으로 AI 인프라 투자 범위가 GPU를 넘어 CPU와 메모리로 확대될 것이라는 기대를 꼽았다. AI 에이전트 서비스 확산으로 AI 수익화 가능성이 높아질수록 하이퍼스케일러의 인프라 투자도 장기화하고 메모리 수요에 대한 가시성 역시 높아질 수 있다는 설명이다. 특히 AI 에이전트는 기존 생성형 AI보다 빈번하고 지속적인 추론 연산을 요구한다는 점에서 메모리 산업에 새로운 수요를 만들 수 있다. AI 모델이 단순히 답변을 생성하는 것을 넘어 여러 단계의 작업을 연속적으로 수행할수록 CPU와 GPU뿐 아니라 HBM, DDR5, eSSD 등 데이터센터 전반의 메모리 사용량이 늘어날 수 있기 때문이다. 김 본부장은 AMD가 미국 반도체 업체 가운데 엔비디아, 브로드컴, 마이크론에 이어 네 번째로 시가총액 1조달러를 넘어선 점도 AI 인프라의 병목이 GPU에서 다른 부품으로 이동하고 있음을 보여주는 신호로 해석했다. 서버용 CPU 출하량이 늘어나면 고용량 DDR5 서버 D램 수요가 확대되고, GPU와 AI 가속기의 증가는 HBM 수요를 동시에 끌어올릴 수 있다는 분석이다. AI 인프라의 성능 경쟁이 연산 능력뿐 아니라 데이터를 얼마나 빠르게 공급할 수 있는지로 이동하면서 메모리의 중요성도 커지고 있다. 김 본부장은 초당 1000토큰 수준의 높은 처리 성능이 요구되는 에이전틱 AI 환경에서는 데이터 공급 속도가 핵심 경쟁력이 될 것으로 봤다. 삼성전자는 이 같은 변화에 대응해 GPU 상단에 메모리를 적층하는 차세대 HBM 기술인 'zHBM' 개발을 추진하고 있으며, 2027년 말 샘플 공급이 예상된다고 김 본부장은 설명했다. 메모리를 단순한 저장장치가 아니라 AI 연산 성능과 효율을 결정하는 핵심 인프라로 보는 시각이 확대되고 있다는 의미다. 김 본부장은 AI 데이터센터를 비유해 GPU가 심장, CPU가 두뇌, 전력이 산소라면 메모리는 데이터를 끊임없이 순환시키는 혈관이라고 설명했다. AI 모델의 규모와 추론 작업이 늘어날수록 데이터 이동량도 증가하는 만큼 메모리의 성능과 효율이 전체 시스템 경쟁력을 좌우할 가능성이 커지고 있다는 것이다. 이 같은 변화가 현실화할 경우 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스는 단순한 메모리 공급업체를 넘어 AI 인프라의 핵심 부품을 제공하는 기업으로 평가받을 가능성이 있다. GPU 중심으로 형성됐던 AI 반도체 투자 사이클이 CPU와 메모리, 저장장치 등으로 확산하면서 국내 메모리 업체들의 실적과 기업가치에 새로운 변수가 될 수 있다는 분석이다. 이상목 기자 mrlsm@etnews.com

items.fullText: 판타지의 경계를 확장하다: 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지가 도쿄게임쇼 2026에서 펼치는 캐릭터 IP와 리테일의 미래 2026/09/23 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 9월 17일부터 20일까지 일본 지바현 마쿠하리 멧세(Makuhari Messe)에서 열린 도쿄게임쇼 2026(Tokyo Game Show 2026, TGS). 글로벌 게임 기업 엔씨 부스는 게임 속 캐릭터를 눈앞에서 만나는 듯한 경험을 하려는 관람객들의 발길이 이어졌다. 그 중심에는 게임의 세계관을 화면 밖으로 확장한 삼성전자의 무안경 3D 디스플레이 ‘스페이셜 사이니지(Spatial Signage)’가 있었다. 이번 행사에서 엔씨가 선보인 ‘아스트라에 오라티오(Astrae Oratio)’는 마법이 일상에 스며든 판타지 세계를 배경으로 한 신전기 서브컬처 RPG다. 삼성 스페이셜 사이니지는 독자적인 ‘3D 플레이트(3D Plate)’ 기술을 적용해 별도의 3D 안경 없이도 콘텐츠에 생생한 입체감을 선사하며, 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 오프라인 전시 공간으로 확장했다. 팬덤 경험 확장… 캐릭터와의 만남을 현실 공간으로 게임 퍼블리셔와 콘텐츠 IP(Intellectual Property, 지식재산권) 보유 기업에게 오프라인 공간은 디지털 콘텐츠를 현실로 가져오는 중요한 접점이다. 엔씨는 도쿄게임쇼에서 85형과 32형 스페이셜 사이니지를 부스 입구와 대기 공간 등에 배치해 관람객이 이동하는 과정에서도 게임 속 캐릭터와 세계관을 자연스럽게 경험하도록 했다. 부스 입구에는 85형 스페이셜 사이니지로 ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 게임의 주요 배경인 ‘특구청’ 건물 내 엘리베이터를 재현했다. 대형 디스플레이를 통해 캐릭터를 실제 사람과 가까운 크기로 표현해, 마치 게임 속 등장인물들이 현실 세계에 인사를 건네는 듯한 장면을 연출했다. ▲ ‘아스트라에 오라티오’ 부스 입구에 설치한 85형 스페이셜 사이니지는 게임 속 다양한 캐릭터가 눈 앞으로 다가오는 듯한 연출로 관람객의 이목을 끌었다. 엔씨 아스트라에 오라티오 사업실 이용수 실장은 “관람객들이 부스에 들어서는 순간부터 실제 크기의 캐릭터와 마주하고 게임 세계에 몰입하길 바랐다”면서 “서브컬처 장르에서는 캐릭터의 생동감과 현실감이 특히 중요한데, 스페이셜 사이니지가 이런 특성을 관람객에게 효과적으로 전달할 수 있다고 판단했다”고 말했다. 현장을 찾은 관람객들은 스페이셜 사이니지가 구현한 캐릭터의 크기와 입체감에 주목했다. 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코(Kawaii CoCo) 씨는 “캐릭터가 실제로 움직이며 상호작용하는 것처럼 생생하게 느껴졌다”며 “일반 디스플레이보다 훨씬 눈에 띄고 소셜미디어에서도 근사하게 보일 것 같아, 이 장면을 촬영해 제 구독자들에게 소개하고 싶다”고 말했다. ▲ 콘텐츠 크리에이터 카와이 코코 씨는 캐릭터의 움직임이 스페이셜 사이니지를 통해 생동감 있게 전달되어 아스트라에 오라티오 부스로 눈길이 갔다고 말했다. 스페이셜 사이니지는 52mm 1 의 얇은 두께에도 불구하고 마치 화면 뒤에 별도의 공간이 있는 듯한 깊이감을 구현한 것이 특징이다. 이러한 경험은 대중에게 게임과 캐릭터의 첫인상을 전달하는 데도 효과적으로 활용될 수 items.fullText: AI Security Is an Engineering Problem — How to Solve It at Every Layer of the Agent Stack Open research, controls across the agent stack and continuous testing help defenders build and operate more secure AI systems. September 21, 2026 by Saša Zdjelar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! AI security is an engineering problem. That means defined security requirements, enforceable controls, named owners and evidence that protections work. As AI becomes more capable, the industry must accelerate security engineering, broaden access to defensive tools and share what works faster. Technology Changes, Security Fundamentals Endure The internet and cloud computing changed how software operates, while core security responsibilities endured: establish identity, control access, limit exposure and verify that protections work. AI agents introduce new capabilities — reasoning, using tools and adapting actions based on the data they encounter. Those capabilities require applying established principles to new operating conditions. This pace creates pressure. Organizations want the productivity benefits of AI while the practices to govern and secure these systems are still developing. Security Depends on the Full Agent Stack Applications depend on code, data, identities, services and infrastructure. Security depends on how those components work together — and AI agents extend that system . Models provide capabilities; harnesses organize context, tools and workflows; and runtime environments provide the infrastructure within which actions execute. Each part of that stack carries security responsibilities, and proper protection requires controls across each layer, as data, instructions and actions move through the system. items.fullText: University of Manchester Uses NVIDIA Earth-2 to Forecast Air Pollution Across the UK Manchester physicists David Topping and Hao Zhang applied NVIDIA Earth-2 generative models to air quality forecasting — unlocking predictions fast enough to inform public health. September 15, 2026 by Isha Salian 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Air pollution is a serious public health risk, contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths in the U.K. alone last year. Data-driven insights can help — but computing air quality with traditional chemistry-based models is expensive, which limits how detailed they can be and how regularly they can be run. David Topping, a professor in the University of Manchester’s department of Earth and environmental science, saw that the NVIDIA Earth-2 family of open AI models and tools had cracked a related problem for weather forecasting — and asked whether the same generative frameworks could work for pollution fields. “The biggest challenge is the compute required to forecast air quality,” said Topping. “Once you put chemistry into weather models, they get really, really slow. So I said, why don’t we try using the generative frameworks that NVIDIA develops for climate and weather for pollution fields?” Working with the NVIDIA Earth-2 team, Topping and colleagues generated training data from existing chemistry-climate simulations, then trained Earth-2 CorrDiff — a generative downscaling model — on Isambard-AI, the U.K.’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol. The model worked on the first attempt. items.fullText: ‘Now We Can Know Everything and Do Anything,’ Jensen Huang Says at Dreamforce At Dreamforce, Salesforce and NVIDIA announced Koa, a CRM reasoning model for Agentforce, post-trained from Nemotron on 27 years of Salesforce CRM intelligence — and running entirely within Salesforce’s own infrastructure. September 15, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Know everything. Do anything. That was the message NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang brought to Salesforce Dreamforce Tuesday, joining CEO Marc Benioff onstage in an appearance that coincided with the announcement of Koa — Salesforce’s first CRM reasoning model, built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super. Huang didn’t just take the stage. He walked into the crowd — threading through the audience at Moscone Center, mic in hand, with Benioff alongside. “We’re all following you, bro,” Benioff told Huang at one point, drawing applause. “With electricity, we could power everything,” Huang said, tracing the arc of industrial revolutions. “With the internet, you can find anything. And now, with artificial intelligence as an infrastructure layer across the planet, we can know everything and do anything.” That arc led directly to the announcement. Salesforce’s first reasoning model was built by post-training NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super on a proprietary synthetic dataset drawn from nearly three decades of enterprise CRM deployments. AI Safety When Benioff asked Huang about AI safety, Huang was direct. “Safety is paramount in a lot of ways. It’s job one,” Huang said. “However, safety is an engineering problem.
